verdict: Darden grew sales 5% to $3.2B with every brand posting higher same-restaurant sales, though profit dipped versus a year ago because that quarter included a $42M gain on selling Olive Garden's Canadian restaurants.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total sales $3.2B, +5.1% vs a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: From continuing operations; $2.04 including discontinued operations

kpis.label: Same-restaurant sales
kpis.note: Blended across all brands, fiscal calendar basis

segments.name: Olive Garden
segments.note: Italian restaurants — Darden's biggest brand. Sales rose 2% as same-restaurant sales grew 1.1% and new restaurants opened (953 locations).

segments.name: LongHorn Steakhouse
segments.note: Steakhouse chain. Sales jumped 11% — same-restaurant sales rose 6.2%, the strongest of any Darden brand, plus new openings (624 locations).

segments.name: Fine Dining
segments.note: The Capital Grille, Ruth's Chris and Eddie V's — the upscale brands. Sales rose 6%, with same-restaurant sales up 1.6%.

segments.name: Other Business
segments.note: Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, Yard House, Chuy's, Seasons 52 and Bahama Breeze. Sales rose 4%, with same-restaurant sales up 3.8%.

opex.name: Restaurant expenses
opex.note: Running the restaurants day to day — rent, utilities, supplies and other site costs.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, kitchen equipment and remodels over their useful lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Head-office costs — management, finance, legal and support for the brands.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promotions to bring guests in.

opex.name: Pre-opening costs
opex.note: Costs of getting new restaurants ready to open — hiring and training before the first guests.

opex.name: Impairment gains, net
opex.note: A small net gain on closing and selling restaurant assets this quarter (a credit, so it reduces expenses).

otherDetail: Other expense of $51M, net: $50M of net interest expense on Darden's borrowings, plus a $1M loss from discontinued operations (the closed Bahama Breeze restaurants, net of tax).
footerNote: Adaptation: for a restaurant company, food & beverage plus restaurant labor are treated as the direct cost of revenue; restaurant expenses, marketing, pre-opening, G&A, depreciation and net impairment gains are shown as operating expenses, mirroring Darden's income statement. Figures are rounded to the nearest $M from the release (sales were $3,200.3M); $1M of rounding was absorbed in restaurant expenses.
oneTimers: A year ago, profit included a $42M gain on the sale of Olive Garden's Canadian restaurants — without it, last year's continuing earnings were $231M ($1.97 per share), so this year's $234M ($2.05) is actually up 4% on a like-for-like basis.

takeaways.title: Every brand grew
takeaways.text: Blended same-restaurant sales rose 3.1%, and all four segments were positive — LongHorn led with +6.2%, Olive Garden added +1.1%. Total sales reached $3.2B, up 5.1%.

takeaways.title: Profit only looks down
takeaways.text: Reported profit fell from $258M to $233M, but last year included a one-off $42M gain on selling the Canadian Olive Gardens. Against last year's adjusted $1.97 per share, continuing EPS of $2.05 is up 4.1%.

takeaways.title: Cash back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Darden bought back $222M of its own shares in the quarter, declared a $1.62 quarterly dividend, and reaffirmed its full-year outlook of $11.10–$11.35 of EPS from continuing operations.
